subject: URGENT: Hightide Commerce — us-west-2 latency & errors / regional fallback
messages:
From: Hightide Ops <ops@hightidecommerce.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara.klein@hightidecommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: us-west-2: 502s + tokenization latency spike — impacting checkout

David —

We started seeing sustained 502s and a sharp latency increase for tokenized checkout requests from 07:55 PDT in us-west-2. Our customers are reporting failed checkouts and order throughput is down ~38% versus baseline. Attached are the last 50 error traces and a short log snippet.

Key symptoms: 502 bursts, client timeouts at 5s, and sequence-length-dependent latency (longer requests have worse tail). Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing regional congestion or a routing issue? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can initiate a cross-region failover to us-east-1 while we investigate.

This is high impact for the July 4th promo window — I have the CFO looped. Please escalate.

— Sara Klein
Head of Site Reliability, Hightide Commerce
Hightide Commerce
Attachments: hightide_error_snippets.txt (text)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Hightide Ops <ops@hightidecommerce.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara.klein@hightidecommerce.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: us-west-2: 502s + tokenization latency spike — impacting checkout

Sara —

Thanks for the rapid heads-up and the traces. We're seeing elevated 5xx counts and KV-cache pressure on several serving clusters in us-west-2 that match your window. I’ve stood up an incident bridge and looped in Engineering (Marissa) and Routing (Laura).

Immediate actions we propose (pending your authorization):
- Trigger geo-steer to fail customer traffic from us-west-2 -> us-east-1 for the public checkout route (can be applied in waves by CIDR).
- Shadow traffic to us-east-1 for 10 minutes to validate quality, then cutover.
- Enable conservative batching and reduce max tokens for checkout models (reduces tail pressure).

Marissa, Laura — can you confirm runtime impact and whether there are any model-compatibility concerns for us-east-1? Sara, please confirm you want us to execute the geo-steer now; if so we'll start the shadow test immediately and send continual updates.

I'll post bridge details in a follow-up.

— David
Principal Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hightide Ops <ops@hightidecommerce.com>, Sara Klein <sara.klein@hightidecommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 08:39:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: us-west-2: 502s + tokenization latency spike — impacting checkout

On Sun, Jul 4, 2027 at 08:28, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa, Laura — can you confirm runtime impact and whether there are any model-compatibility concerns for us-east-1?

Checked cluster telemetry. Root cause appears to be a combination of KVCACHE saturation on a subset of us-west-2 nodes + an anomalous kernel scheduling path that increases token latency for sequence lengths > 140. We have a short checklist in the runbook for this: warm up alternative model replica, apply conservative batching config, and route heavy sessions to dedicated pool.

Technical plan (ready to execute):
1) Attach: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook excerpt).
2) Shadow 10% of checkout traffic to us-east-1 for 5 minutes, validate 200/latency SLA.
3) If good, ramp to 100% over 6 minutes with circuit-break guard.
4) Post-cutover: keep KV-cache priming scripts running for 12 hours and keep batch size conservative for 24 hours.

Risks: slight model-version mismatch for a rare candidate reranking variant — we will pin to the verified production replica in us-east-1 and run a quick smoke on holdings. No schema or function-calling changes expected.

Requesting sign-off from Hightide on the shadow test and exec visibility for any credit conversation.

— Marissa
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf (PDF)

Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: us-west-2: 502s + tokenization latency spike — impacting checkout

David / Marissa —

Please proceed with the shadow test immediately. Our checkout traffic mix is critical for the next 90 minutes; the sooner we get traffic stabilized the better.

Two asks from Hightide:
1) ETA for full 100% cutover if the shadow is healthy.
2) A preliminary view on credits for the outage window (we will have finance on the bridge).

We authorize Redwood to execute the geo-steer and conservative batching. Keep the CFO posted on any material time-to-repair.

— Sara
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara.klein@hightidecommerce.com>, Hightide Ops <ops@hightidecommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Hightide — executive update & authorization log

Team —

Exec note for records and C-suite: we executed the agreed plan at 08:45 PDT (shadow test start), observed a 92% success rate with median p50 latency improved from 1.4s -> 0.42s on shadowed traffic, and no functional regression. Ramp to 100% began at 08:55 and completed at 09:01. Service error rate in us-west-2 dropped to baseline as traffic drained; us-east-1 carried steady load.

Actions taken:
- Geo-steer applied and validated (cutover complete at 09:01).
- Conservative batching + token limit applied for checkout route.
- KV-cache priming job started and will run 12h.
- Postmortem ticket created and assigned to Marissa (INC-2027-HTD-67).

Customer request: Hightide CFO asked for an initial credit assessment. Sean, can you prepare a one-page credit memo and estimated token-usage cost delta for the affected window? Laura, please attach the routing-change log to the HubSpot case.

Sara — please confirm once accounting has the ask and we'll coordinate the credit conversation.

I'll convert this thread into a short incident summary and send to both boards.

— David
Principal Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
